items.q: The ancient Greeks thought amber was made from drops of solid water.
Amber comes from trees that lived millions of years ago.
The resin helped seal the wound and protect the tree.
The little fly escaped from the resin.
The resin became amber in a few years.
Under ultraviolet light, some rare amber may glow bright blue.

options: A thick, sticky liquid from a tree
items.why: “A thick, sticky liquid began to flow from the wound. This liquid was called resin.”

items.q: What was the resin like for the tree?
items.why: “It was like a bandage made by the tree itself!”

items.q: What landed on the golden resin?
items.why: “One sunny morning, a little fly landed on the golden resin.”

items.q: What made the buried resin harder and more stable?
items.why: “Chemical changes made it harder and more stable.”
“Most amber looks yellow, orange, or golden brown.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Amber comes from the resin of trees that lived millions of years ago. Sometimes a little insect got stuck in the sticky resin. The resin hardened, stayed under the ground for millions of years, and slowly became amber with the insect still inside.

items.q: Why did the tree make resin?
items.model: Its bark was damaged. The resin helped seal the wound and protect the tree.

items.q: What happened to the resin after the old tree fell?
items.model: It reached the forest floor. Soil and sand slowly covered it, and it stayed hidden deep beneath the ground. Over millions of years, it changed and became amber.

items.q: Why is amber important for scientists?
items.model: Scientists can study the insects, spiders and plant pieces preserved in amber. They help us learn about ancient life.

items.q: If you could make a time capsule, what would you put inside it?
